newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYMEAL AND SOYOIL END HIGHER ON DRY FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYMEAL AND SOYOIL END HIGHER ON DRY FORECAST.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended higher on Wednesday, in line with gains in soybeans, on weather forecasts that suggested weekend rains would again bypass dry pockets of the U.S. Midwest, traders sadi.

Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist David Taylor said Wednesday that showers forecast for the U.S. Midwest this weekend may be lightest in the areas where corn and soybean crops need them most. WSC predicted 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain this weekend with 40 to 60 percent coverage.
That outlook differed from other forecasts issued early in the week calling for widespread weekend rains.
There was also talk on the trading floor that other meteorologists had reduced rainfall amounts and coverage in their weekend forecasts.
The soy complex had incurred heavy losses earlier this week amid ideas weather patterns were looking wetter.

Agronomists said soybeans were not permanently damaged during July, which was one of the driest on record, but moisture was vital during August when soybeans fill pods. Late season stress can also lower oil content, they said.
Soymeal ended $4.40 to $1.90 per ton with December up $3.90 at $214.10. Soyoil closed 0.41 to 0.34 cent per lb higher with December up 0.41 at 22.75 cents.
On the day, Tenco Inc bought 500 lots December soymeal and sold 300 while ING and FIMAT Futures each bought 400 December, traders said.
In soyoil, Produce Grain bought 500 December and 100 September while ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp and Iowa Grain each bought 200 December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 15,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 17,311 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 23,000 lots, against Tuesday's 19,597.
